source_text: Confessus es ergo aliter operari gratiam in maioribus, aliter in minoribus. Nec quidquam putes responsioni tuae relictum loci, si inferas magnam quidem, sed in remissione peccatorum esse distantiam, ut, etsi unum peccatum, tamen inveniat, quod remittat. Verum nihil hac argumentatione promoves; neque enim refert, in qua specie varios unius gratiae fatearis effectus, dummodo varios posse esse fateare.
pass_a_gloss: You have therefore confessed that grace works otherwise in the greater, otherwise in the lesser. Nor should you think any place left to your response, if you infer that there is indeed a great distance, but in the remission of sins, so that, even if one sin, it nevertheless finds what it may remit. But you advance nothing by this argumentation; for it does not matter in which species you confess varied effects of one grace, provided you confess that they can be varied.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: You have therefore confessed that grace operates one way in older people and another in younger ones. Do not imagine any room remains for your answer if you add that the difference is indeed great, but concerns the remission of sins, so that it still finds a sin to forgive, even if only one. This argument advances nothing. It does not matter under what heading you acknowledge different effects of one grace, provided you acknowledge that its effects can differ.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
In this book Julian usually means the Savior's gift abounding against Adam's sin (Rom 5), not later system-grace as a substance, and not 'favoritism' unless a suum-cuique definition is in play.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
